channel_name: Invest Like the Best · Patrick O'Shaughnessy
video_title: How He Built the World’s Largest Digital Bank with 140 Million Customers
gist: Nubank's founder-CEO (spoken as 'New Bank') argues digital banking is under 10% of a $10 trillion industry, citing a cost to serve about 3% of incumbents, a proprietary credit foundation model, a December 2025 AI inflection that led to rebuilding 120 workflows and flattening from 10 layers to 5, plus the US launch and a 35-country stablecoin account.

insights.claim: New Bank serves about 140 million customers with 10,000 employees, versus incumbent competitors with about 100 million customers, 100,000 employees and 6,000 branches, giving a cost to serve roughly 3% of a traditional incumbent bank before any AI benefit.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Structural cost gap is the core of the margin and pricing-power case for digital banks over branch-based incumbents.
insights.quote: our cost to serve a customer is about 3% of what a traditional income bank is

insights.claim: Global consumer financial services is roughly a $10 trillion industry, about 90% of which still runs through branches and incumbents; all neobanks and fintechs together hold under 10%, comparable to Netflix when most people still used Blockbuster.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Frames fintech as early-innings share migration plus market expansion, countering the 'fintech is saturated' view.
insights.quote: we are you are all of those fintexs and all these new banks together and we're less than 10% of that entire market

insights.claim: New Bank is described as the only neobank worldwide to have fully surpassed the largest incumbent in its home market: close to 120 million Brazilian customers (over 65% of adults), with about 60% using it as their primary account.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Primary-account status rather than secondary wallet implies deposit and cross-sell economics are real; replicating in Mexico and Colombia is the test.
insights.quote: we become the primary bank account of the entire country

insights.claim: Because New Bank charges essentially no fees, it has lower revenue but a return on equity two to three times that of incumbent banks in its markets, which management treats as proof of a cost-structure moat.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: ROE vs incumbents, alongside customer growth, NPS and LTV/CAC, is the metric set the CEO wants analysts to use.
insights.quote: we end up with a return on equity that is two to threex their return on equity

insights.claim: Some US incumbent banks now earn higher ROE than emerging-market banks New Bank competes with, which the CEO reads as large margin to undercut even in the US.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: High incumbent profitability is the target for the US launch; implies fee and deposit-yield pricing pressure on US banks if it works.

insights.claim: About 70% of deposits at big incumbent banks in Mexico and Brazil pay zero, with the 30% that earns yield going mostly to high-income customers and corporates.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Free deposit funding is the incumbents' key subsidy; open-banking-enabled switching threatens it.

themes.theme: Access, cost and intelligence: the three profit-pool disruptions

insights.claim: The CEO frames financial services problems as access, cost and intelligence: roughly three billion people lack access to credit, and even Mexico and Colombia have only about 13% credit card penetration.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: A TAM framework for emerging-market consumer credit growth underpinned by data, underwriting and digital rails.

insights.claim: US retail deposits of about $15 trillion earn roughly 40 basis points on average; at 4.5-5% rates the gap is about $600 billion a year that effectively pays for branches and that digital banking could return to consumers.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Sizes the deposit-yield profit pool at risk for US banks if digital competitors pass yield through.
insights.quote: there's about 15 trillion dollars of retail deposits in the US banking system, but banks pay on average about 40 basis point on yield a year

insights.claim: Remittances (about $100 billion leaving the US at 5-10% per transaction) and monthly account fees of $5-15 are cited as cost pools that competition will push toward zero, since moving money is just moving bits.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Fee compression risk for remittance providers and fee-reliant banks.
insights.quote: that will go to zero remittances moving money is you're moving bits that will trend towards zero

insights.claim: Financial education never solved the intelligence gap for ordinary people; AI can give everyone the equivalent of a private banker that optimizes deposits, taxes and loan shopping, competing away profit pools that exist because customers lack advice.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Consumer AI agents are a disintermediation threat to fee and spread revenue at incumbents.
insights.quote: You're not going to solve this problem of intelligence through education. You can solve it through AI.

insights.claim: Open banking plus AI lets a provider see a customer's accounts elsewhere and act proactively; New Bank already tells about 15 million Brazilian customers daily when another bank's credit card bill is due with no funds, offering money to pay it or refinancing a 10% loan at 5%.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Shows how cross-institution data turns into proactive refinancing that attacks incumbents' penalty-rate and interest profit pools.

insights.claim: Inertia, not product quality, keeps customers at incumbents; in a commoditized banking product the best no-fee product should win nearly all share, and open banking with AI is what reduces that inertia.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Switching-cost erosion is the mechanism for share shift, so watch open-banking implementation and AI agent adoption.

insights.claim: Humans will still matter for roughly 5% of cases such as mortgages, small business relationships and wealthy investors, but savings accounts, cards and loans no longer need physical branches.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Supports the view that branch networks are structurally redundant for the bulk of retail products.

themes.theme: AI moats, data and org redesign

insights.claim: Even if an AI-native startup attacks New Bank with speed, it faces regulatory barriers (banking licences take two to three years and cannot be generated by ChatGPT) plus a data gap; New Bank has 20 to 30 thousand data points per customer across 13 years.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Licences, data, brand and trust are the incumbent moats that AI does not erode, favoring scaled digital natives over pure startups.
insights.quote: you still cannot really get Chad GPT to get you a banking license

insights.claim: New Bank bought Hyperplane, a Palo Alto foundation-model startup struggling with two-year sales cycles to incumbent banks, and built what it believes is the first proprietary financial-services foundation model for credit decisions, now also used for fraud and for day-one underwriting in new markets.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Proprietary foundation models on own data support faster international expansion and better credit and collection decisions.

insights.claim: Scale and data are not sufficient: Blockbuster had abundant customer data but lacked systems and data culture, whereas Netflix built a better algorithm from none; incumbents still run 15 systems from acquisitions and are mid-migration off COBOL and mainframes.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: The advantage is systems and culture; incumbent legacy tech stacks are a drag on their AI adoption.

insights.claim: The foundation model cut the cost of testing new features in credit models from months of work to fast experiments, so many organizational decisions can be automated by models rather than humans.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Speed of model iteration compounds the data advantage in credit.

insights.claim: New Bank tested coding models on Clojure through 2025 with poor results until Opus 4.6 arrived in December 2025; leadership noticed about 60 days late, then ran a reinvention mapping 120 workflows across the company to be rebuilt natively with AI, with eval infrastructure.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: A concrete timeline for when frontier coding models crossed a usability threshold for a niche language and triggered enterprise-wide process redesign.
insights.quote: we use a lot of closure as a as a as a programming language

insights.claim: AI-driven reorganization took the CEO from 1 to 20 direct reports and the organization from 10 management layers to 5, using a proactive company-brain information system and direct skip-level contact to reach ground truth.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Evidence for flatter AI-enabled organizations and middle-management compression.

insights.claim: AI will reinvent HR: daily Olympic-athlete-style coaching for engineers, designers and PMs through AI copilots reviewing pull requests and work, and real-time team instrumentation for managers, replacing six-month, recency-biased reviews.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Workforce performance management is an underdiscussed AI application area.
insights.quote: the opportunity that ultimately AI is going to create for every single person in organization is you have Olympic athlete type of coaching

insights.claim: The CEO argues that AI increases the case for in-person work: individuals working alone at home compete directly with AI and lose, while collaboration and coordination in presence is the distinctly human work; New Bank moved from remote to hybrid with much more office time.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Counters the remote-work-plus-AI narrative; relevant to office demand and company culture trends.

insights.claim: New Bank requires senior managers to build real software products every quarter and the CEO personally coded a non-custodial crypto app in an afternoon, tracking AI progress mainly via X and a personal summarizing agent.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Shows management hands-on AI usage as an adoption tactic.

insights.claim: Most AI discourse focuses on efficiency and optimization while neglecting customer obsession; prioritizing customer value over short-term fee income when it is inconvenient is where humans still beat AI.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Companies using AI to extract fees rather than serve customers may face trust problems.

insights.claim: AI agents will become a customer segment to be marketed to, with a dedicated team and agent-SEO, but banking will still require human trust and brand since people care where life savings sit; New Bank also plans an open agent that offers third-party products.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Agentic commerce will reshape distribution but trust-heavy categories keep brand relevance.

themes.theme: Structural shifts: cash, open finance, stablecoins

insights.claim: The end of cash in cash-heavy economies like Mexico, Indonesia and parts of Africa, via real-time payment systems such as Pix and UPI, removes branch needs and creates transaction data that enables credit for people previously invisible, such as a taco stand in Mexico City.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Digital ledger formation is a precondition for credit expansion; real-time rails are catalysts for neobank growth.

insights.claim: About 70% of Brazilian employment is in small businesses, similar to India and Southeast Asia; digitizing their cash flows could enable trillions of dollars of credit for billions of people.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Small-business credit is the biggest unlocked lending pool in emerging markets.

insights.claim: Open finance lets consumers carry data history between providers and even monetize it, loosening incumbent inertia in an oligopoly where five or six US banks own 60-70% of assets, and implying a more fragmented banking industry with lower fees.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Open-banking rules are a catalyst for bank concentration to decline over time.

insights.claim: The CEO predicts the roughly 190 world currencies shrink to about 10 over 10-20 years because many fiat currencies are effectively tokens under dire fiscal conditions, with billions banking offshore in US stablecoins and Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Bold long-term view on currency substitution; implies demand for dollar stablecoins in emerging markets.

insights.claim: US dollar stablecoins democratize access to the dollar and will help keep it the reserve currency for a long time, though it will share the role with perhaps five or six fiat currencies and a few crypto tokens; the US fiscal position is bad but better than most emerging markets.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Stablecoins are framed as dollar-supportive demand, and Bitcoin as a portfolio diversifier.

insights.claim: Creditworthiness can be created: New Bank was the first credit card for 30 million people in Latin America, starting with $20 lines that grew to $100 and then $1,000, plus an AI copilot coaching customers to improve credit.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Small-ticket graduated credit builds customer histories that incumbents dismissed as absurd.

insights.claim: New Bank is launching in the US and offering a stablecoin-backed account across upwards of 35 countries, arguing its 2013 seed deck was a global thesis about digital-native retail banking rather than a Brazil-specific one.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Marks the shift from a three-country LatAm story to global expansion; a key catalyst for the next growth leg.

insights.claim: Hardest part of the US launch is building a brand and trust organically and capital-efficiently rather than spending heavily on marketing, as US consumers weigh brand in choosing banks.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: US customer acquisition cost is the key execution risk to watch.

insights.claim: Expansion learning: Brazil was largely banked, so Mexico's initial cash culture made competing harder; as countries digitize, markets homogenize like social media, Netflix, Spotify and Uber. New Bank became the second largest bank in Mexico.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Digital-native advantage grows as cash declines, but offline markets slow entry.
insights.quote: We're I always say that we are a we're a shark in digital waters.

insights.claim: Bear case for New Bank: Brazil, Mexico and Colombia saturate with 65% of Brazil already a customer, growth declines, international expansion fails and AI opportunities are missed; bull case is 100+ countries and a cost structure about 50x better than the industry that owns 90% of a $10 trillion profit pool.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Management's own scenario bookends: international growth is the swing factor.
insights.quote: Very soon we're going to run out of Brazilians.

insights.claim: Fintech investing is shifting toward larger scaled neobanks that combine AI transformation with data, brand and licences; entering consumer fintech with hundreds of millions of customers is harder for new startups unless fundamentally different, with early entrants more likely to be AI applications.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Capital is concentrating in scaled fintech winners rather than seed-stage consumer fintech.

insights.claim: Founder and CEO are different roles: founders are impatient with urgency and are better as individual contributors, CEOs are patient systems builders; the guest prefers to remain more founder, claiming founder-led companies outperform for decades, especially in big technology shifts.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Supports a premium for founder-led companies in technology transitions.
insights.quote: founder companies continue to outperform for decades

insights.claim: Great leadership requires a differentiated vision, the ability to sell it against 'it's not realistic' reactions, and the humility to navigate between pure revolution and consensus, since status quo elements exist for evolutionary reasons.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: The leadership model behind the company's contrarian bet on beating incumbents.

insights.claim: The guest argues AI makes finding a mission harder because the bar to start is lower, and the best founders are now pursuing seemingly impossible problems such as hardware and space.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Observation that startup talent is rotating toward hard-tech areas as software gets easier.

insights.claim: For ten years local experts said New Bank would be crushed by incumbent banks; it later passed several incumbents in Brazil to become the largest private financial institution on the continent, and launched in Colombia with an event of 100,000 viewers.
insights.speaker: New Bank founder/CEO (guest)
insights.so_what: Incumbent skepticism consistently underestimated cost-structure disruption.
